===Alternative forms===
* {{alter|en|musick|musicke|musique}} (obsolete)

===Etymology===
{{root|en|ine-pro|*men- (think)}}
From {{inh|en|enm|musik}}, {{m|enm|musike}}, borrowed from {{der|en|xno|musik}}, {{m|fro|musike}}, {{der|en|fro|musique}}, and their source {{der|en|la|mūsica}}, from {{der|en|grc|μουσική}}, from {{der|en|grc|Μοῦσα||Muse}}, an Ancient Greek deity of the arts. {{surf|en|muse|-ic|t2=pertaining to}}. In this sense, displaced native {{cog|ang|drēam||music}}, whence {{w|Modern English}} {{m|en|dream}}. Fully displaced {{ncog|ang|sweġl}}.

===Noun===
{{en-noun|-|s}}

# A [[series]] of [[sound#Noun|sounds]] [[organize]]d in [[time#Noun|time]], usually [[employ#Verb|employing]] some [[combination]] of [[harmony]], [[melody]], [[rhythm]], [[tempo]], [[timbre]], [[sound design]], [[lyrics]], etc., often to [[convey]] a [[mood]].
#: {{ux|en|I keep listening to this '''music''' because it’s a masterpiece.}}
#* {{RQ:Congreve Mourning Bride|page=1|passage='''Muſick''' has Charms to ſooth a ſavage Breaſt, / To ſoften Rocks, or bend a knotted Oak.}}
# {{lb|en|figuratively}} Any [[interesting#Adjective|interesting]] or [[pleasing#Adjective|pleasing]] sounds.
# {{senseid|en|Q638}}An [[art form]], [[create]]d by organizing [[pitch#Noun|pitch]], rhythm, and sounds made using [[musical instrument]]s and/or [[singing#Noun|singing]].
# A [[guide#Noun|guide]] to [[play#Verb|playing]] or [[sing#Verb|singing]] a particular [[tune#Noun|tune]]; [[sheet music]].
# {{lb|en|military|slang}} [[electronic|Electronic]] [[signal#Noun|signal]] [[jamming#Noun|jamming]].
# {{lb|en|US|slang|dated}} [[heated#Adjective|Heated]] [[argument#Noun|argument]].
# {{lb|en|US|slang|dated}} [[fun|Fun]]; [[amusement]].
